xenophon.s: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier, historian and philosopher of the late fifth and fourth centuries BCE, a pupil of Socrates. He served with the Greek mercenaries hired by Cyrus the Younger in 401 BCE and led their retreat after Cyrus's death.

xerxes-i.s: Xerxes I was king of the Achaemenid Empire from 486 to 465 BCE, the son and successor of Darius I. He led the great invasion of Greece in 480 BCE, which won at Thermopylae and sacked Athens but was defeated at Salamis and, in 479 BCE, at Plataea.

xianbei.s: The Xianbei were a nomadic people of the eastern Eurasian steppe, in present-day Mongolia and Manchuria. After the decline of the Xiongnu, they became the dominant power on the northern steppe in the second century CE.

xiang-army.s: The Xiang Army was a regional military force raised in Hunan province by the scholar-official Zeng Guofan to fight the Taiping Rebellion. Its success, together with Li Hongzhang's Huai Army, was crucial in suppressing the Taiping.

xiang-jun.s: The xiang jun was the professional standing army of the Song Dynasty. The Song Dynasty profile notes that it was very large, with estimates of over one million men under arms at its peak.

xiang-yu.s: Xiang Yu was a Chinese military leader who led the rebellion against the Qin dynasty and became the dominant warlord after its fall. He then fought Liu Bang for control of China in the Chu–Han contention.

xiangyang.s: Xiangyang is a city on the Han River in central China, which with its twin city Fancheng formed the gateway to the Yangtze valley. The Mongol siege of Xiangyang from 1267 to 1273 was the pivotal confrontation in the conquest of the Southern Song.

xing-ware.s: Xing ware is a type of white porcelain produced at kilns in northern China under the Tang Dynasty. Its fine white body made it one of the earliest high-quality porcelains.

xinhai-revolution.s: The Xinhai Revolution was the revolution of 1911 that overthrew the Qing Empire and ended imperial rule in China. It was triggered by a military mutiny at Wuchang and spread rapidly as provinces declared independence.

xinjiang.s: Xinjiang is a large region in north-western China, including the Tarim Basin and Dzungaria, historically home to oasis cities on the Silk Road. Its eastern parts formed part of the domains of the Chagatai Empire and its successors.

xiongnu-civil-war.s: The Xiongnu civil war was a succession conflict among rival claimants to the position of chanyu that split the Xiongnu Empire around 57 BCE. The confederation divided between factions led by Huhanye, who submitted to the Han Dynasty, and his brother Zhizhi, who moved westward.

xiongnu-empire.s: The Xiongnu Empire was a confederation of nomadic peoples that dominated the eastern Eurasian steppe from the late third century BCE to the first century CE. Under the chanyu Modu it united the steppe tribes and became a formidable rival of the Han Dynasty, extracting tribute…

xoconusco.s: Xoconusco, or Soconusco, is a region on the Pacific coast of southern Mexico, in modern Chiapas, renowned for its cacao. The Aztec Empire profile records that the ruler Ahuitzotl extended the empire south to Xoconusco and into what is now Guatemala.

xuanwu-gate-incident.s: The Xuanwu Gate Incident was a palace coup in 626 CE in which Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers, the crown prince Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, at the Xuanwu Gate of the Tang palace in Chang'an. His father, Emperor Gaozu, soon abdicated in his favour.

xwastak.s: Xwastak was the land tax of the Sasanian Empire. The Sasanian Empire profile explains that the fiscal system rested on this tax, assessed on agricultural production.

xiao-baojuan.s: Xiao Baojuan was emperor of the Southern Qi dynasty from 498 to 501, posthumously demoted to Marquess of Donghun. His reign was remembered for extravagance and the killing of ministers, generals and relatives.

xue-ju.s: Xue Ju was a wealthy local leader of Jincheng, modern Lanzhou, who rebelled in 617 as the Sui dynasty collapsed and proclaimed himself emperor of Qin. His armies controlled much of Gansu and defeated the young Tang prince Li Shimin in 618, but Xue Ju died soon afterwards.

xue-rengao.s: Xue Rengao was the second and last ruler of the short-lived Qin state founded by his father Xue Ju in the north-west during the collapse of the Sui dynasty. He succeeded in 618 after Qin had beaten Tang forces at Qianshuiyuan, but later that year Li Shimin, the future Emperor…

xanana-gusmao.s: Xanana Gusmão is an East Timorese independence leader who commanded the Fretilin resistance against Indonesian occupation from 1981 until his capture in 1992. After the 1999 independence referendum he became the first President of East Timor in 2002 and later served as prime…

xavier-coppolani.s: Xavier Coppolani was a Corsican-born French colonial administrator and scholar of Islamic brotherhoods. From 1902 he pursued a policy of peaceful penetration in Mauritania, using alliances with religious leaders to bring the emirates of Trarza and Brakna under French…

xi-gui.s: Xi Gui was the wife of the Marquis of Xi, a small Zhou state, whose story is told in the Zuo zhuan. An insult to her by the Marquis of Cai drew Chu into the region; King Wen of Chu destroyed Xi around 680 BCE and took her as his wife, and by tradition she bore him the future…

xia-yue.s: Xia Yue was the deputy through whom Chen Yu, chief minister of Zhao, governed the Kingdom of Dai after the fall of the Qin. In 205 BCE the Han general Han Xin defeated and captured him, opening the way for the destruction of the Zhao army at Jingxing the following year.

xiao-cong.s: Xiao Cong was the third and last emperor of the Western Liang, a client state at Jiangling on the middle Yangtze. In 587 Emperor Wen of Sui summoned him to Chang'an and abolished the state; Xiao Cong was given a noble title, and his sister was the empress of Emperor Yang of Sui.

xiao-daocheng.s: Xiao Daocheng was a general who became the power behind the Liu Song throne in southern China. In 479 he forced Emperor Shun to abdicate and founded the Southern Qi dynasty, reigning as Emperor Gao until 482 and attempting to restore order to state finances.

xiao-defei.s: Xiao Defei was the wife of Yelü Chun, the Liao prince proclaimed emperor at Yanjing in 1122, founding the Northern Liao. After his death within months she governed as empress dowager, but when the Jurchen ruler Aguda took Yanjing at the end of 1122 she fled and was later…

xiao-he.s: Xiao He was the chancellor of Liu Bang, founder of the Han dynasty. He secured the Qin archives when the rebels took Xianyang, kept the armies supplied from Guanzhong and Sichuan during the war with Xiang Yu, and as first chancellor of the Han drafted its laws on Qin models.

xicotencatl-the-elder.s: Xicotencatl the Elder was one of the four rulers of Tlaxcala in central Mexico. After Tlaxcala fought Hernán Cortés in 1519, he and Maxixcatzin led its alliance with the Spaniards, supplying thousands of warriors for the conquest of Tenochtitlan, while his son Xicotencatl the…

xu-shouhui.s: Xu Shouhui was a leader of the southern Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan dynasty. In 1351 he proclaimed the Tianwan regime on the middle Yangtze, but power passed to his officer Chen Youliang, who murdered him in 1360 and founded the Chen Han state, prompting commanders…

xu-wen.s: Xu Wen was a general of the Wu kingdom of the Ten Kingdoms period. After Yang Xingmi's death he seized control of the government from the weak Yang heirs and ruled as regent, while his adopted son Xu Zhigao ran affairs from Jinling; in 937 Xu Zhigao took the throne and founded…
